# Enable Inner Site Access

## Goal

Let employees access ERP, CRM, order systems, or internal admin consoles through Sa2web.

Each frontend user has an independent remote browser profile for inner sites. If user A accesses and logs in to an inner site, user B will not inherit user A's login state when accessing the same inner site. Their browser data remains isolated.

## Confirm Network Reachability

The inner site URL must be reachable from the deployment environment or browser node.

Sa2web does not replace underlying network connectivity. The browser node still needs the required routing, intranet tunneling, DNS, firewall, and ACL conditions to access the internal system.

## Add an Inner Site

Go to:

```text
Site Management > Inner Site List
```

Open the Sa2web inner site list, as shown in @fig-inner-site-list.

![Sa2web inner site list](/images/inner-site-list.png){#fig-inner-site-list}

Click **Add Site** to open the add inner site dialog, as shown in @fig-add-inner-site-dialog.

![Sa2web add inner site](/images/add-inner-site-dialog.png){#fig-add-inner-site-dialog}

Fill in:

- Name.
- URL.
- Description.
- Logo.

## Group Authorization

Authorize the inner site to business users in a group.

Go to:

```text
Group Management > Inner Sites
```

Open the inner site authorization page, as shown in @fig-inner-site-group.

![Sa2web inner site authorization](/images/inner-site-group.png){#fig-inner-site-group}

Select the inner sites that need authorization, then click **Save**.

After authorization, users can click **Enter** in the **Internal Systems** area of the frontend, as shown in @fig-inner-site-access.

![Sa2web inner site access](/images/inner-site-access.png){#fig-inner-site-access}

## Typical Remote Work Path

```text
Employee normal browser
   ->
Sa2web
   ->
Enterprise-side browser runtime
   ->
ERP / CRM / internal backend
```

With this path, employee devices do not need to connect directly to inner sites, and internal system addresses do not need to be exposed.

## Acceptance Checklist

- [ ] The browser node can access the internal URL.
- [ ] Authorized users can see the inner site.
- [ ] Unauthorized users cannot see it.
- [ ] External devices do not need direct connectivity to the inner site.
